payload.transcript: Today I want to look at how cities manage heat. Urban areas are often several degrees warmer than the surrounding countryside, a phenomenon known as the heat island effect. The main culprit is not traffic or air conditioning, as many people assume, but the materials we build with. Dark asphalt and concrete absorb sunlight during the day and release it slowly after sunset, so nights remain uncomfortably warm. Some planners have responded by painting roofs white, which reflects light effectively and is cheap. However, my own view is that planting trees is the better long term investment, because shade also cools the pavement beneath it and trees add moisture to the air. The drawback is time. A sapling takes roughly twenty years to provide meaningful cover, whereas a coat of reflective paint works within a week. For that reason, I would argue that the sensible strategy combines both, using paint immediately and trees for the future. Next week we will turn to the question of water, and I will ask you to read the short paper on reservoirs before the seminar.
payload.question: According to the lecturer, what chiefly causes cities to stay warm at night?
options: Heavy traffic on main roads
The use of air conditioning
Building materials that store and slowly release heat
A lack of rainfall in summer
payload.explanation_uz: Ma'ruzachi sababni transport yoki konditsioner emas, balki qurilish materiallari deydi: asfalt va beton kunduzi issiqni yutib, kechasi sekin chiqaradi.

payload.transcript:
A: Doctor Karim, your new book argues that teenagers should start school later. Why?
B: Because adolescent body clocks shift. Around puberty the brain releases the sleep hormone about two hours later than in children, so asking a fifteen year old to concentrate at eight in the morning is like asking an adult to work at six.
A: Some headteachers say a later start simply pushes everything back, and students stay up even later.
B: That was my worry too, but a trial in twelve schools showed otherwise. Pupils slept an extra hour on average, and attendance rose noticeably.
A: Were exam results better?
B: Honestly, the improvement was modest, and I would not oversell it. What surprised me more was that teachers reported fewer arguments in the corridors.
A: So what is your advice to parents who cannot change the school timetable?
B: Keep screens out of the bedroom. Light from phones delays the hormone even further, and that is something families can control tonight.
payload.question: What did the trial in the schools show?
options: Pupils went to bed later than before
Attendance fell slightly
Exam scores rose sharply
Pupils slept about an hour longer on average
payload.explanation_uz: Matnda: "Pupils slept an extra hour on average" - o'quvchilar o'rtacha bir soat ko'proq uxlagan.

payload.transcript: Good morning. Commuters in the northern region face disruption this week as engineers begin replacing the railway bridge at Elmsworth. The work, which was originally planned for next spring, has been brought forward after inspectors found cracks in the central supports. Trains will not run between Harbridge and Dunmore until the end of the month, and replacement buses will leave every twenty minutes. The operator admits the buses will add roughly forty minutes to the average journey, and has urged passengers to consider working from home where possible. Local business owners are less than pleased. One cafe owner told us that she expects to lose a third of her trade, since most of her customers arrive by train. The transport minister, however, insisted that safety must come first and ruled out any compensation for shops. Meanwhile, cyclists have welcomed the news, as the council has promised to open a temporary path along the river by Friday. We will bring you updates throughout the day.
payload.question: Why was the bridge work brought forward?
options: Commuters complained about delays
The budget was approved early
The council wanted a cycle path
Inspectors found damage to the supports
payload.explanation_uz: Matnda: "inspectors found cracks in the central supports" - ustunlarda yoriqlar topilgan.

payload.transcript:
A: Good afternoon, how can I help?
B: Hello, I booked a double room for three nights, but I've just realised I entered the wrong dates. I arrive on the fourteenth, not the twelfth.
A: Let me see. Yes, I can amend that, though I should mention that the rate is lower for the earlier dates, so the new price will be slightly higher.
B: How much higher?
A: About fifteen pounds a night. Alternatively, there's a room with a garden view, which is still available at the original price.
B: That sounds better. Is breakfast included?
A: Only on the premium rate. Otherwise it's eight pounds per person.
B: I'll skip breakfast, then. I'd rather find a cafe nearby.
A: There's a good bakery two minutes down the road. Now, could I take a card number to hold the booking?
B: Of course, but I'd prefer to pay on arrival.
A: That's no problem, we only need the details as a guarantee.
payload.question: Why is the guest calling?
options: To cancel the booking
To correct the dates of a reservation
To complain about the price
To ask for a breakfast discount
payload.explanation_uz: Mehmon: "I entered the wrong dates" - sanalarni noto'g'ri kiritgan, shuning uchun tuzatmoqchi.
